 David Raya injury news, latest update as Arsenal star forced off vs Newcastle
 By
 Joe Prince-Wright , 
 By
 Joe Prince-Wright 
     Published November 21, 2026 02:03 PM 
 Add 
 on Google 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Email
 Add 
 on Google 
 Arsenal fans will be sweating on the latest David Raya injury news, with their star goalkeeper coming off against Newcastle on Saturday and it didn’t look great. 
 With Arsenal under pressure after coughing up a 1-0 half-time lead and trailing 2-1 early in the second half , this was the last thing Mikel Arteta needed. 
 Even though they recovered after Raya’s injury and fought back to make it 2-2. 
 Aside from the result Arteta will be very concerned about Raya, who was subbed off looking in real pain, with Kepa Arrizabalaga coming on in his place. 
 David Raya latest injury news, update
 A high ball into the box put Raya under pressure and he seemed to collide pretty innocuously with Newcastle striker William Osula. 
 But Raya immediately reacted and went down needing treatment. 
 NEWCASTLE UPON TYNE, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 21: William Osula of Newcastle United reacts towards David Raya of Arsenal who appears to be injured during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Newcastle United and Arsenal FC at St James’ Park on November 21, 2026 in Newcastle upon Tyne, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images)
 Getty Images
 After treatment on the pitch he was then helped off by Arsenal’s medical staff, as he walked off the pitch supporting his left arm after previously looking to be holding his shoulder. 
 Kepa Arrizabalaga is a fine back-up goalkeeper, but if Raya (the winner of the Premier League’s Golden Glove award in three of the last four campaigns) is out for a long period of time, this will be a huge problem for Arsenal. 
 We will provide the latest David Raya injury news and update from Mikel Arteta after the game at St James’ Park. 
 NEWCASTLE UPON TYNE, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 21: David Raya of Arsenal is helped to his feet by teammate Bruno Guimaraes and medical staff after sustaining an injury during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Newcastle United and Arsenal FC at St James’ Park on November 21, 2026 in Newcastle upon Tyne, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images)
